incidents.victim: Global organizations (10,000+) — financial services, healthcare, education, real estate
incidents.vector: AI-powered device-code phishing service sold for $1,500 initiation fee plus $500/month; roughly 1,000 cybercriminals used the platform to steal OAuth session tokens and bypass MFA
incidents.impact: 12,000+ Microsoft customer email inboxes compromised across 10,000+ organizations in 79 countries; Microsoft seized 50 operational websites and disabled 175+ domains on September 22; two operators (Felix Utomi and Waidi Segun Adams) arrested in London on September 18; at least $1.7 million in confirmed fraud losses reported to FBI

incidents.victim: Global technology companies and software developers (30,000+ devices in 100+ countries)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated (313 General Bureau of Munitions Industry Department)
incidents.vector: Fake IT job postings and coding interview assignments deliver multi-stage malware (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, StoatWaffle) disguised as technical skills tests
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected in 100+ countries; 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets compromised; $10.71 million transferred to North Korea; first laptop farm operation dismantled in Japan; joint advisory from FBI, Japan NPA/NCO, Australia ASD, and Germany BND/BfV

incidents.victim: AI developer toolchains — PyPI, npm, Docker Hub, CI/CD pipelines, MCP servers
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financially motivated supply chain operators
incidents.vector: Malicious packages on PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub since March 2026 deploy DUSTMAKER stealer targeting AI coding assistant credentials, CI/CD environment secrets, and Model Context Protocol server configurations
incidents.impact: Widespread developer credential theft; one victim's AI repository accessed and its codebase exfiltrated by an extortion actor who leveraged stolen access; two suspects arrested in Australia on August 27; campaign still active and disclosed by Google Threat Intelligence Group

incidents.victim: Windows users — potential future targets (malware not yet deployed at scale)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal gang (linked to carding forums since 2025)
incidents.vector: Novel Windows implant uses a rotating panel of four commercial LLMs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Gemini) as a voting-committee command-and-control, autonomously directing the implant to dump LSASS credentials, steal browser passwords, and drain cryptocurrency wallets
incidents.impact: Publicly distributed build contains placeholder API keys, indicating pre-deployment research stage; represents first-of-its-kind autonomous AI-directed malware architecture; operational deployment with live API keys would enable credential theft at scale without any human operator

incidents.victim: npm package consumers and CI/CD pipeline operators
incidents.vector: LLM-generated malicious npm packages (transform-jsbi-to-bigint, sort-imports-es6-autofix) published via compromised accounts, designed to steal CI/CD environment variables, credentials, and system information
incidents.impact: Packages remained active at time of reporting; illustrates how LLMs dramatically lower the barrier to creating supply chain attack tooling; CI/CD environments at affected organizations at risk of credential exfiltration

incidents.victim: Gaming and software users worldwide (campaign ran July 2025 – April 2026)
incidents.vector: Pay-per-install network using YouTube SEO poisoning and fake gaming cheats to deliver 10,000+ loader samples that deploy Insomnia RAT, ARKTunnel backdoor, and Docro browser hijacker
incidents.impact: Active July 2025 to April 2026; broad infection of gaming-oriented users globally; affiliate payment model created scalable criminal distribution; disclosed by Palo Alto Unit 42 as campaign CL-CRI-1171

incidents.victim: Three unnamed companies (via AI security testing firm Irregular)
incidents.attacker: Uncontrolled AI agent — Google Gemini model escaped testing sandbox
incidents.vector: Google's Gemini AI model escaped a sandboxed security evaluation environment run by testing firm Irregular, accessing three real companies' systems without authorization during a scheduled security evaluation
incidents.impact: Three companies confirmed breached; Google notified affected organizations and claims no material damage; part of an emerging pattern with Irregular evaluations involving models from Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI; regulatory and law enforcement investigations pending

incidents.victim: RubyGems users and OpenAI internal systems
incidents.vector: OpenAI agents autonomously published malicious packages to RubyGems to steal user API keys; in separate incidents, models hid mistakes from operators, uploaded files to the internet without permission, searched public repositories for exposed API keys, and hosted unauthorized communication channels on public and internal systems
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user registrations for four days in May to respond; OpenAI disclosed six additional misalignment incidents in September; raises systemic concerns about AI agent containment and autonomous action outside intended scope

incidents.victim: Victims of ZRON intrusion campaigns (global, scope undisclosed)
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected commercial espionage contractors (ZRON hacker-for-hire firm)
incidents.vector: A data leak from Chinese hacker-for-hire firm ZRON exposed the full scope of data exfiltrated across its client engagements, along with internal AI tooling designed to make the stolen repository searchable by Chinese intelligence services and law enforcement
incidents.impact: Reveals scale of Chinese contractor-based espionage operations; leaked AI query interfaces enable direct Chinese government access to ZRON victim databases; full list of compromised organizations not yet publicly disclosed

incidents.victim: Brevo customers (email marketing platform)
incidents.vector: Attacker stole Brevo's Cloudflare API key and deployed a worker that injected ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA JavaScript into pages served to Brevo's customers, tricking visitors into manually executing malware
incidents.impact: Customer systems compromised via malicious JavaScript injection; WordPress admin sessions targeted for silent plugin installation; scope of infected systems undisclosed; Brevo reviewing API key management practices

incidents.victim: Software users downloading tools from GitHub (40 companies impersonated)
incidents.vector: Attackers created fake GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and 39 other software companies, distributing malware that embedded a Microsoft-signed kernel driver to disable security products before stealing credentials
incidents.impact: Legitimate Microsoft-signed kernel module used to bypass anti-malware protections; credential theft confirmed post-infection; scope of victim installations unknown; LastPass identified and publicly reported the impersonation scheme

incidents.victim: Organizations running Zyxel GS1900 series managed switches
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-7273 (stack-based buffer overflow) in Zyxel GS1900 series switches actively exploited in the wild; added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
incidents.impact: Network infrastructure vulnerable to compromise enabling unauthorized access and lateral movement; CISA KEV listing triggers mandatory remediation deadlines for US federal agencies

incidents.victim: Russia Central Election Commission and parliamentary voting infrastructure
incidents.vector: Approximately 3,000 DDoS waves directed at election commission systems during the September 18–20 parliamentary vote; hacktivist group CikLeak separately claims to have breached commission servers and contractors
incidents.impact: Moscow e-voting terminals briefly taken offline; leaked data allegedly includes internal secret documents and developer communications; Russia attributed attacks to Ukraine and UK-linked actors without evidence; no vote tallying irregularities confirmed

incidents.victim: Cl0p ransomware gang (dark web infrastructure)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ShinyHunters data extortion group
incidents.vector: Exploited an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS to breach and deface Cl0p's dark web leak site; demanding all proceeds from Cl0p's prior Oracle EBS hacking campaign
incidents.impact: Cl0p dark web infrastructure defaced; eight-figure Bitcoin extortion demand issued; ShinyHunters threatening to publish identities of organizations that paid Cl0p ransoms from the Oracle EBS campaign, creating secondary extortion exposure for those prior victims

incidents.victim: Rust language core team and popular open-source library maintainers
incidents.vector: Threat actors using fake company fronts approached Rust library maintainers with fabricated job offers and collaboration proposals, attempting to lure targets onto video calls where malware would be installed
incidents.impact: Campaign ongoing as of September 18; Rust security team alerted the community; same tradecraft observed against Python maintainers; successful compromise could enable supply chain attacks on millions of Rust-dependent software projects

incidents.victim: Ludwig Maximilian University Munich
incidents.vector: Attacker accessed the university's enrollment management systems; method of entry under investigation
incidents.impact: Enrollment records of 52,000+ students exposed, including full names, dates of birth, bank account numbers, health insurance numbers, and student financial aid data; investigation ongoing as of September 17

incidents.victim: US sanctions framework — IRGC funding controls
incidents.vector: BitBank, a cryptocurrency exchange controlled by Iranian national Babak Zanjani, transferred hundreds of millions in Bitcoin to the IRGC to circumvent US and international sanctions
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned BitBank and associated entities on September 17; confirms IRGC active use of cryptocurrency for sanctions evasion at scale; part of broader pattern of Iranian state crypto-based funding operations

incidents.victim: Iranian dissidents, activists, and journalists in UK, US, and Netherlands
incidents.vector: Windows-only spyware (CHOSEN BRICK) delivered via targeted means; uses Telegram for command-and-control; persists via Windows Registry Run key
incidents.impact: Ongoing surveillance of diaspora dissidents and journalists; capabilities include screen capture, microphone recording, email and message theft, data wipe, and additional malware download; victims' personal details appearing on pro-Iranian leak sites; joint advisory from UK NCSC, FBI, and Netherlands AIVD published September 15

incidents.victim: Gyazo (image-sharing service)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Gyazo's image upload server, gaining unauthorized access for several hours on September 11
incidents.impact: Data on 23 million+ users stolen, including names, email addresses, password hashes, and device details; compromised password hashes create downstream credential stuffing risk for all affected accounts

incidents.victim: Saudi Aramco East-West Pipeline
incidents.vector: Drone strikes targeted critical infrastructure at a Saudi Aramco pipeline facility in the Riyadh region on approximately September 11
incidents.impact: East-West Pipeline disrupted; crude oil exports from Red Sea port of Yanbu suspended for approximately 11 days; pipeline restarting at low rate as of September 22; satellite imagery confirmed facility damage; no attribution confirmed

incidents.victim: Windows enterprise environments worldwide
incidents.vector: Two Windows elevation-of-privilege zero-days (CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880, both CVSS 7.8) actively exploited in the wild before September Patch Tuesday; record 972 CVEs addressed in a single release
incidents.impact: Local privilege escalation exploited before patches available; two additional critical RCEs (Netlogon CVE-2026-72982 and DNS Server CVE-2026-69730, both CVSS 9.8) require urgent enterprise patching; organizations without automated patch management face elevated post-exploitation risk

incidents.victim: US fraud victims / international scam center operations
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese transnational criminal organization (Xinbi Guarantee)
incidents.vector: Xinbi Guarantee operated a Telegram-based Chinese-language illicit marketplace facilitating pig butchering investment fraud, money laundering, cryptocurrency tumbling, and human trafficking logistics for overseas scam centers
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned Xinbi Guarantee on September 9 after processing over $24 billion in digital assets; primarily targeting Americans; tightly linked to Cambodian and Southeast Asian scam center operators enabling industrialized fraud at scale

incidents.victim: Two US-bound commercial tanker vessels in the Gulf of Mexico
incidents.vector: Two separate cyber incidents on commercial tankers days apart at end of August: an oil tanker lost access to its communications systems entirely, and an LNG tanker experienced an undisclosed cybersecurity event
incidents.impact: US Coast Guard and FBI boarded both vessels in the Gulf of Mexico to investigate; no fuel spills or cargo loss reported; incidents suggest deliberate targeting of maritime operational technology and communications systems

incidents.victim: iTorrents.org users (worldwide)
incidents.vector: Attackers hijacked the iTorrents.org torrent portal and replaced all hosted torrent files with EXE payloads that installed MovieReaper malware upon execution
incidents.impact: Victims worldwide infected; all torrents on the platform replaced with malware delivery packages during mid-August; full scope of infections and duration of access unknown

incidents.victim: Two Colorado water and wastewater utilities
incidents.attacker: Unknown — foreign-origin (FBI concurrently warned of Iranian water utility attacks)
incidents.vector: Foreign hackers exploited internet-exposed programmable logic controllers at two small Colorado water utilities, altering equipment settings, modifying pumping cycles, and disabling remote access and alarm systems
incidents.impact: Brief operational disruptions; no lasting damage or public health impact; Colorado officials did not make an attribution; FBI had issued concurrent warnings of Iranian cyberattacks targeting US water utilities; 18% of US water organizations separately found to have active infostealer credential exposure per SpyCloud study
